modelNotes: Minutes Engine 1.1 uses player-pool status plus season, last 5, and last 10 minutes from NBA history.
Unknown starters retain their historical minutes baseline and are not treated as confirmed bench players.
Missing injury information does not mean a player is cleared; publication eligibility requires confirmed game status and role.
Roles are Core Starter, Starter, Rotation, Bench, Deep Bench, and Inactive.
No odds or betting lines are used.

injury.shortComment: Drummond (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Heat.
injury.detail: Drummond played just nine minutes prior to exiting Wednesday's 121-102 win over Cleveland due to a concussion. Mohamed Diawara and James Wiseman will likely get a boost in playing time off the Knicks' bench with Drummond sidelined. His next chance to suit up will come against the Hawks on Sunday.

injury.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injury.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injury.shortComment: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injury.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injury.shortComment: Mathurin (foot) is doubtful for Friday's game against the Clippers.
injury.detail: Mathurin has been dealing with plantar fasciitis for quite some time and hasn't suited up in any of the Pelicans' last six games. The doubtful tag leaves the door open for a potential return, but it wouldn't be surprising if he remains sidelined. Mathurin is averaging just 5.5 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game this season.

injury.shortComment: Youngblood (heel) is out for Friday's game against the Warriors.
injury.detail: Youngblood is in line for a ninth straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Sunday against the Pelicans.

injury.shortComment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
injury.detail: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

injury.shortComment: Lillard (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors. The veteran guard is dealing with right calf tightness and soreness.
injury.detail: Lillard's absence creates additional ball-handling and scoring opportunities for Jrue Holiday and Deni Avdija, while Scoot Henderson could see increased playing time. Lillard's next opportunity to return comes Sunday against New Orleans.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Robinson (quadriceps) is out for Friday's game against the Bucks.
injury.detail: Robinson is carrying a day-to-day tag due to a left quadriceps strain, but the veteran sharpshooter is not ready to play yet and will miss a sixth consecutive game Friday. This means Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Harper (hip) participated in Friday's morning shootaround, per Matt Guzman of SI.com.
injury.detail: Harper appears to be making swift progress in his recovery from a hip strain, which has cost him just around one week after initially being expected to hold him out for multiple weeks. The star guard can be tentatively placed on the right side of his questionable tag for Friday's showdown against the Lakers.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: The Pistons announced Tuesday that Okorie (oblique) will miss at least two weeks, per Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com.
injury.detail: Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injury.detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
injury.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Detroit recalled Duren (hamstring) from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Wednesday.
injury.detail: Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

injury.shortComment: Landale (hip) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
injury.detail: Landale won't suit up Friday and this will be his fifth consecutive absence. His next chance to play will come against the Knicks on Sunday.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Clarkson (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Heat.
injury.detail: Plantar fasciitis is costing Clarkson a fifth consecutive contest Friday. His next chance to suit up arrives Sunday against the Hawks.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Jakucionis (ankle) won't play Friday's game against the Pistons.
injury.detail: Jakucionis will miss his second game of the season due to left ankle tenosynovitis. In his absence, Ryan Rollins, Caris LeVert and AJ Green could see expanded roles, while rookie Brayden Burries should also get a slight bump in minutes.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address swelling in his left knee, and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Ball (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies. The guard was previously questionable after spraining his left ankle during Wednesday's win over Oklahoma City.
injury.detail: With Ball and Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland should handle increased ball-handling responsibilities. Minnesota's depleted backcourt could also create additional scoring opportunities for Jaden McDaniels. Ball's next opportunity to return comes Monday against Sacramento.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: Robinson has been ruled out Marc D'Amico of the Celtics' official sitefor Friday's game.
injury.detail: Neemias Queta should continue handling the bulk of Boston's center minutes, with Luka Garza and Chris Cenac potentially receiving additional opportunities. Robinson's next chance to return comes Sunday against the Spurs.

injury.detail: Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

injury.shortComment: Anunoby (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Heat. The forward was previously listed as doubtful and will miss his third consecutive contest due to a left calf strain.
injury.detail: Landry Shamet could remain in the starting lineup, while Josh Hart may absorb additional responsibilities on the wing. Anunoby's return to on-court activities is encouraging, but his next opportunity to play comes Sunday against Atlanta.

injury.detail: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

injury.detail: Pippen hasn't been available for Memphis since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a clear timeline to return. He can be deemed week-to-week going forward, though his absence could extend into mid-December if the Grizzlies don't advance in the NBA Cup.

players.statusSource: ESPN team roster; game availability not confirmed

injury.shortComment: De Larrea (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Suns.
injury.detail: De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.
